what: Which production serving settings keep vLLM's exact tier? Qwen3-8B (BF16, thinking off), vLLM 0.32.0, VLLM_BATCH_INVARIANT=1, a rented 2x RTX 4090 box (Quebec, driver 580.178.04). Each setting made a determinism run (48 prompts, max 200 tokens, greedy, sequential and 16 concurrent; vllm_determinism.py) compared with the eager baseline; one-pass referee checks (vllm_onepass_referee.py) of compiled-mode runs; and the llmverify logits processor under n-gram speculative decoding, its receipts checked by a plain eager referee (vllm_exact_receipts.py).

vs_eager_baseline.tensor parallel 2, eager: its own group: 28 of 48 replies diverge from TP=1; batch-invariant within itself (sequential = concurrent)
vs_eager_baseline.CUDA graphs + n-gram speculation, TP=1: differs from eager and from graphs without speculation

eager_baseline_reproducible: a second eager server after a toolchain change, and the earlier RTX 4090 run on another box, both match the eager baseline at all 8,250 positions

compiled_mode.across restarts: not reproducible: three compiled server starts (a fresh compile, a compile with the cache cleared, a start reusing the compile cache) produced 8,288, 8,261 and 8,271 tokens and diverged on 29-36 of 48 replies from each other
compiled_mode.one-pass referee: fails: an eager referee's prefill differs from compiled decode at 8,287 of 8,288 positions; a compiled server's own prefill differs from its decode at 8,067 of 8,288

rule_under_speculative_decoding.what: llmverify/vllm_rule.py now masks every logits row (one per draft position) to the rule's choice for its own step; receipts from a server with the rule and n-gram speculation (mean acceptance length 1.09), checked by a plain eager referee without speculation

verdict: For an exact one-pass tier on vLLM: batch-invariant mode, --enforce-eager, a fixed tensor-parallel size (part of the tier), any prefix caching / chunking / n-gram speculation. CUDA graphs with torch.compile give numbers that are stable within one server lifetime but change on every restart, so no referee can reproduce them; a provider in that mode falls to the statistical tier. Which of compilation or graph capture causes it was not separated.

throughput_rtx4090.what: output tokens/s, Qwen3-8B, 256-token replies, vLLM 0.32.0, one rented RTX 4090 (performance only; this box's numerics were faulty, see below)
throughput_rtx4090.note: the cost of exactness on a dense model is batch-invariant mode itself (about 2x), eager vs compiled is 2-5%. On gpt-oss-20b (MoE, Marlin MXFP4) batch-invariant mode cost nothing measurable at 16 concurrent.

faulty_machine.what: one rented RTX 4090 (driver 615.71.09) gave different numbers on different server starts in batch-invariant eager mode: four distinct results in eight starts (two separately installed environments), none matching the canonical numbers that every other Ampere/Ada machine reproduced
faulty_machine.control: a second RTX 4090 on the same driver 615.71.09 reproduced the canonical numbers exactly on three starts (0 of 8,250 positions differ), so the driver is not the cause; it was that machine
faulty_machine.consequence: a split of compiled mode into compile-only and graphs-only, run on that machine, is inconclusive and not reported; the compiled-mode finding above comes from a machine whose eager runs were reproducible
faulty_machine.lesson: an exact tier needs admission and periodic calibration: a node runs a fixed probe whose canonical answers are known, and hardware that does not reproduce them stays in the statistical tier instead of being penalized
